units.source_excerpt: After that, two specific types of transition curve, quarter circle and quarter ellipse, are introduced to calculate the optimal design. Then we further develop the 2D quarter-ellipse model into a more actual and complex case, involving the third dimension of the halfpipe.
units.function: Show how a simple geometry becomes a higher-dimensional design model.
units.reusable_pattern: After comparing {candidate_models}, we extend {selected_model} from {simple_setting} to {realistic_setting}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call added dimensions more realistic unless their role is modeled.

units.source_excerpt: We analyze the problem from the viewpoint of energy translation. We build a simple quarter circle-type model to study what factors involve in and what role they play. Next the sliding process is further simulated by introducing an elliptic-type trail.
units.function: State the analytical viewpoint and preview the baseline-to-extension route.
units.reusable_pattern: We analyze {problem} through {viewpoint}, begin with {baseline} to isolate {factors}, and then introduce {extension}.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use a roadmap as a substitute for the task deliverables.

units.source_excerpt: Before calculation, several assumptions are made for simplicity. With these assumptions, we build our basic model, make force analysis, set up kinematical equations and obtain the general form of final mechanical energy analytically.
units.function: Compress assumptions, mechanics, equations, and analytical output.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: In the quarter-ellipse model, we obtain analytical solutions and find the best radius for the circle. While in quarter-ellipse model, we use numerical simulation to get the optimal semi-major and semi-minor axes.
units.function: Contrast analytical and numerical branches on a shared design output.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: By introducing the sensitivity coefficient into these models, the sensitivities of different variables are analyzed both qualitatively and quantitatively.
units.function: Preview the local-sensitivity layer after model selection.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: At last, the tailors and tradeoffs to develop a practical course are discussed. The shape of the halfpipe is further optimized with construction difficulty, players' safety and performance taken into consideration.
units.function: Move from energy optimum to three practical criteria.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: In conclusion, through systematic and comprehensive analysis of various factors, we find a reasonable shape of the snowboard course, which fits the real data well.
units.function: Close with a selected design and an evidence claim requiring calibration.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: There are three main tasks in this paper: determine the shape that generates the highest jump, optimize the shape for other trick requirements, and state what properties should be abandoned.
units.function: Translate the prompt into three ordered design tasks.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The competition between gravitational potential energy and losses caused by friction and collision determines sliding. We first consider 2D, build a quarter-circle model, introduce an elliptic trail, and calculate energy loss numerically.
units.function: Explain why the model sequence follows the energy balance.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Then we take the third dimension into consideration and consider slope angle by balancing energy gaining and losing. At last, construction difficulty, player safety and performance are added.
units.function: Complete the roadmap from 2D energy to 3D and practical decisions.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The symbol table separates geometry, mechanics and initial conditions: mass, friction, pressure, total energy, halfpipe height, landing distance, initial height and energy, width, half width and length.
units.function: Group symbols by model role before equations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The cross-section diagram places deck, bottom, vertical wall, transition, width, half width and height in one coordinate view before the symbols are used.
units.function: Bind notation to a visual geometry.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: We treat the snowboarder as a mass point, ignore body twists and other geometrical properties, and constrain the point to move on the snowboard course.
units.function: Bound the moving object and trajectory.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Only collision and sliding friction account for mechanical energy loss, the halfpipe is perfectly rigid, the player falls from hi with zero initial velocity, and the collision is perfectly inelastic.
units.function: Collect the energy and impact assumptions before the ODE.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The mass-point assumption is used mainly to simplify calculation and focus on the essential interaction between course shape and maximum vertical air; twist and rotation are deferred.
units.function: Justify a simplification by the retained decision.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The course is assumed rigid because deformation happens over a very short downhill travel and a constructed snow course should support the rider without frequently deforming.
units.function: Give physical and operational reasons for a boundary assumption.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The profile phi(x) defines the halfpipe; frictional loss, normal force, curvature and mechanical energy are combined into an ordinary differential equation for E.
units.function: Assemble geometry and mechanics into the state equation.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The landing point and collision angle set a perfectly inelastic post-collision velocity and initial mechanical energy before the profile ODE is solved.
units.function: Attach an event condition to the continuous energy model.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Because final energy is a functional of the profile and its derivatives, the paper limits the feature of phi(x) and reduces the variational problem to lower-dimensional curve families.
units.function: Explain why unrestricted shape optimization becomes a family search.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: A vertical wall, horizontal path and quarter circle form the first-order approximation. The circle gives a closed-form energy relation and a one-dimensional search over radius.
units.function: Introduce a solvable baseline curve family.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The quarter ellipse introduces semi-major axis a and semi-minor axis b. Forward Euler propagates the energy equation and bisection is used to obtain the best axes.
units.function: Move from a one-parameter analytical family to a two-parameter numerical family.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The paper first ignores collision loss and keeps only sliding friction. The resulting axes tend toward zero, which is used to argue that collision loss is essential.
units.function: Use a negative ablation to justify a model component.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Restoring collision creates an interior peak for a at fixed b, while energy increases as b grows; the best pair is obtained by comparing peak values.
units.function: Show how the restored component changes the design landscape.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Air resistance proportional to speed is added under a low-speed assumption. Alpha is varied from 0 to 1.5 with windward area and other parameters fixed.
units.function: Add one physical loss term with an explicit sweep and fixed controls.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: A dimensionless local sensitivity coefficient is introduced so six inputs can be compared on a common response scale.
units.function: Define a common local response metric before ranking factors.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The downhill slope adds gravitational gain. A coordinate transformation maps the sloped course to a 2D section so the existing energy model can be reused.
units.function: Extend dimension through a transformation and explicit reuse.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The suitable slope is defined by equal hanging height on both sides; cubic-spline interpolation of final height versus slope gives the intersection with the initial-height line.
units.function: Turn a practical criterion into an interpolated root.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Theoretical energy design is explicitly separated from the later safety, construction and twist adjustments.
units.function: Mark the boundary between physical optimum and multicriteria design.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The quarter-circle plots compare best radius with width, friction, initial height and landing position, reporting constant width response, inverse friction direction, a rough height gradient and a landing-position boundary.
units.function: Report four factor directions under one curve family.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: For hi=9.0 m, x0=0.5 m, mu=0.1 and w=9.0 m, the reported best radius is 3.831 m.
units.function: State the complete scenario before the optimum.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: With collision omitted, final energy is maximized as either ellipse axis tends toward zero, producing an unreasonable right-angle trail.
units.function: Preserve a degenerate negative result and its consequence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Under h0=5.4, hi=9.0, x0=0.5, mu=0.1 and alpha=0.75, the reported best ellipse is (a*,b*)=(4.19,5.4).
units.function: Tie the selected ellipse to its parameter block.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The paper reports local coefficients for x0, hi, alpha, h0, mu and Ei, while b remains at the height boundary.
units.function: Preserve all local coefficients before interpreting factor importance.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: A steeper slope requires smaller a while b remains h0. The local slope sensitivity is -0.4605 at 17 degrees.
units.function: Report the 3D response direction and local coefficient.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Cubic-spline interpolation gives slope 17.1 degrees where final hanging height equals 9.0 m, with corresponding ellipse axes (4.42 m,5.4 m).
units.function: Report criterion, interpolation, root and geometry together.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Safety and construction arguments adjust the theoretical slope from 17.1 to about 17.5 degrees and the edge angle from nearly 90 to about 85 degrees.
units.function: Separate theoretical output from qualitative practical adjustment.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Because b* always equals halfpipe height, the paper estimates sensitivity only for a* across landing point, initial height, air damping, pipe height, snow friction and initial energy.
units.function: State the fixed response and six perturbed dimensions.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The reported coefficients are 0.552, -2.110, 0.011, 2.374, 0.993 and -2.110 at the selected baseline points.
units.function: Keep the complete local response vector.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The sensitivity plots are one-factor local curves; no joint uncertainty, alternate geometry family or decision reversal is tested.
units.function: Delimit local sensitivity from robustness.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Edge angle should be neither too large nor too small: larger angles reduce holding force, while smaller angles increase landing shock. The cited operating interval is 83 to 88 degrees.
units.function: Frame safety as a two-sided design tradeoff.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Larger slope gives higher jumps and higher danger, so the slope is increased only slightly; the bottom segment is retained to give the player preparation time despite friction loss.
units.function: Show two practical departures from the energy optimum.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: A near-vertical edge is difficult to hold snow on, so decreasing the edge angle also serves construction requirements.
units.function: Add constructability as an independent criterion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: More time in the air and a safer side wall support twists, leading to a bounded increase in slope and a side-wall angle below 90 degrees.
units.function: Translate an athletic task into two design directions.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The paper credits its staged architecture: a simple basic model followed by corrections, rather than one complex model with all variables together.
units.function: Name staged construction as a model-interface strength.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The strengths list systematic factor coverage, fit of halfpipe size and slope to real data, visual relation plots, a general ellipse family and quantitative sensitivity coefficients.
units.function: Inventory positive artifacts by function.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The weaknesses retain omitted rotation and twist, a fixed velocity direction, and the possibility that the ellipse family does not maximize vertical air.
units.function: Name omitted physics, path restriction and family risk.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: The conclusion recaps the energy viewpoint, basic interaction model, force analysis and general analytical energy expression before the design branches.
units.function: Reconstruct the dependency chain before final values.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present a selected scenario as a universal optimum.
Preserve omitted physics, parameter provenance, and validation scope.

units.source_excerpt: Quarter-circle analytical optimization is followed by quarter-ellipse simulation, sensitivity, 3D slope extension and practical tradeoffs in the same order as the body.

units.source_excerpt: The final reported design is a=4.42 m, b=5.4 m and slope 17.5 degrees, after the theoretical slope has been adjusted by practical requirements.
